text:
Predicates:
Book(x) ::: x is a book.
Contains(x, y) ::: x contains y.
Knowledge(y) ::: y is knowledge.
Person(x) ::: x is a person.
Reads(x, y) ::: x reads y.
Gains(x, y) ::: x gains y.
Smarter(x) ::: x is smarter.
Premises:
∀x (Book(x) → ∃y (Knowledge(y) ∧ Contains(x, y))) ::: Books contain tons of knowledge.
∀x ∀y ((Person(x) ∧ Book(y) ∧ Reads(x, y)) → Gains(x, knowledge)) ::: When a person reads a book, that person gains knowledge.
∀x (Gains(x, knowledge) → Smarter(x)) ::: If a person gains knowledge, they become smarter.
Reads(harry, walden) ∧ Book(walden) ::: Harry read the book “Walden” by Henry Thoreau.
Conclusion:
Contains(walden, knowledge) ::: Walden contains knowledge.
